text: Dear love, just a gentle note. Your payment didn't go through this month, because the purse was a bit light.
No fuss. The interest keeps ticking, mind, so pop into any branch when you're flush and I'll sort you out. Pat.
Dear love, that's two months now. I'm not cross. I've seen far worse, and one of them was a vicar.
But it does cost you more each month you leave it. Even a bit paid off helps. Pat.
Dear love, three months behind. This is the firm letter, so I'm writing it in capitals, which doesn't suit me.
NOBODY IS COMING TO TAKE ANYTHING. But please do come and see me. Kettle's on. Pat.
Dear love, that's your loan paid off in full. Not a penny owing.
You can borrow again whenever you like, within reason. But I do hope you don't need to. Pat.
Love, I've put a few quid in with this, for the road. Three hundred. It's a sub, not a present, so keep count.
No interest, I'm your mother. But I'll be remembering it every time I look at that kettle. Pay me back when you're flush. Mum x
Love, I'm not saying anything. I'm just saying that Auntie Val got her sub back within the week.
I'm sure yours is on its way. Mum x

talk.apr: Here's the plain version. A loan costs a rate every month, on whatever you still owe. Left alone for a year, that adds up to more than twelve times the monthly rate, because interest is charged on the interest. The law makes me print that yearly figure, and call it the APR.
talk.early: Pay it off early and you only pay for the days you had the money. I don't charge a penny for finishing early.
talk.savings: Savings pay a little, on what's in the account across the month. Not much. It's not a lottery ticket, it's a mattress with manners.
